conviction_note: The findings are small and point both ways. Peer and dealer proxies lean slightly negative: Cars.com's Q3 today showed a lower dealer count, revenue tracking toward the low end of its guide and soft dealer media, and CARG's own sequential dealer adds have slowed to +33. Against that sit a strong upside skew (-25 vol pts), short interest that rose 23% to 10.7% of shares, and new monetisation products, so p_up 48 on an abs move of 10 gives -0.4, close to impact_sum -0.7. The print turns on the Q4 guide, which no source pre-announces.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus ~$256.4-256.9M (Benzinga $256.4M https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CARG/earnings-forecasts ; MarketBeat $256.9M https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/cargurus-nasdaqcarg-issues-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-08-06/), inside the company guide of $253.5-258.5M revenue, $82-90M adj. EBITDA and $0.63-0.69 non-GAAP EPS on 90.0M shares (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001494259/000119312526338014/carg-ex99_1.htm, 2026-08-06). The EPS consensus is disputed: $0.61 (MarketBeat), $0.64 (Benzinga), $0.68 (Chartmill). FY2026 guide: revenue +10-13% on FY2025's $907.0M, with the adj. EBITDA margin 0.5-1.5pp below 2025 (raised in August from 1.5-2.5pp below). Arithmetic: Q3 2025 revenue was $232.1M (907.0 - 433.8 H1 2025 - 241.1 Q4 2025), so the Q3 guide midpoint is about +10.3% YoY, after +15% in Q1 and +13% in Q2. The FY range implies Q4 2026 revenue of $247-274M (+2.5% to +13.8% YoY, midpoint about $261M). No sourced Q4 consensus was found.
positioning_check: Short interest was 9,492,243 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, up from 7,729,497 (+23%), equal to 10.7% of shares outstanding, with 5.03 days to cover. The model estimate for 10-30 is 9.83M (source: https://equibles.com/stocks/carg/shortinterest, read 2026-11-05). An earlier snapshot showed 5.5 days to cover (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/CARG/). The 25-delta skew is -25.42 vol pts, so the market is paying for upside; the ATM spread is 76% of mid, so the 13.52% event-implied move is indicative only. Run-up is +22.3% over 20 days and +10.0% over 5 days, 8.4% below the 52-week high. The 2026-11-04 jump (+8 to +12.7% depending on source) came on volume 58% below average, with no company news, and was attributed to a sector-wide rally in digital platforms (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-cargurus-nasdaq-carg-stock-price-up-127-heres-what-happened-2026-11-04/). The short is building and moderately crowded, not extreme.

findings.finding: Cars.com, the closest US listings peer, reported Q3 2026 before the open on 2026-11-05. Dealer customers were 19,251, down 92 Q/Q and 275 YoY. Revenue was $181.9M against a ~$183M consensus (a slight miss), dealer revenue rose only 1%, and the outlook cited 'pressure in Dealer and OEM media products amid current market conditions'. Management said FY revenue will land toward the lower end of its flat-to-+2% guide. Q3 traffic was -4% YoY but +5% Q/Q, and leads were up nearly double digits. CARS shares were flat on the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CARG's last four prints moved +7.16% (Aug 2026, when the FY margin guide was raised), -8.95% (May 2026, in line with the margin-compression guide reiterated) and +3.32% / +0.63%. The stock trades on the forward guide and on margins, not on peers. No record was found of how CARG reacted to Cars.com prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The release came out this morning, about 10 hours before CARG reports, and CARG fell ~1.6% today (equibles close $35.93) after a +22% 20-day run-up. If the market had read it as a sector warning, CARG would have given back more of the 11-04 sector-rally gain. Cars.com has been losing dealers to CarGurus for years, so the read-through is weak.
findings.independence: Call commentary from the same company (https://gloom.sh/stocks/cars/transcripts/q3-2026) says revenue is 'toward the lower end'; it shares the source, so it is not independent. StockStory reports the revenue miss and flat shares (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/cars/news/earnings/carscom-nysecars-misses-q3-2026-revenue-estimates). It is a peer proxy, not CARG's own number.

findings.finding: Dealer economics in Q3 2026 were mixed but profit-supportive. AutoNation used retail units fell 5% to 65,410 while used GPU rose to $1,524 from $1,489. Lithia same-store used retail units fell 3.2% while used retail GPU rose ~11% to $1,970. Cox: September used retail sales were +2% YoY, and days' supply rose from 44 to 49 (inventory +3.9% M/M). Carvana posted record retail units of 217k (+39% YoY). Higher dealer gross per unit and rising days' supply support listing and marketing spend, while lower franchise volumes and Carvana's share gains weigh on dealer budgets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved record links CARG's reactions to industry used-car series. Its subscription revenue (QARSD +8% US in Q2) has grown through both soft and firm unit markets.
findings.why_not_priced: These are broad, public series, so mostly priced. If the market read them as a strong dealer tailwind, the skew and run-up would already show it, and the skew does lean up.
findings.independence: AutoNation Q3 2026 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000350698/000162828026068579/an-20260930.htm); Lithia per GoodCarBadCar (https://www.goodcarbadcar.net/?p=100458); Carvana Q3 release (https://finviz.com/news/410551/carvana-announces-record-third-quarter-2026-results). Each is a separate company document. All are proxies, and they point in mixed directions.

findings.finding: CarGurus' own paying-dealer adds have slowed sharply: 34,409 at Q4 2025, 34,596 at Q1 2026 (+187) and 34,629 at Q2 2026 (+33). US dealers were 26,151 (+3% YoY) and international 8,478 (+11%). With Cars.com losing 92 dealers Q/Q in Q3, a flat or negative sequential CARG dealer count is plausible, and Q2's revenue growth came mainly from QARSD (+7%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 had +33 dealer adds and a QARSD-led beat, and the stock rose +7.16% because the margin guide was raised. On this print the dealer-count line was outweighed by guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: The trend is in public releases, but previews quote revenue and EPS, not dealer count. A market positioned for a dealer-count disappointment would not be paying 25 vol points for upside.
findings.independence: The Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 counts come from StockStory (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/carg/news/earnings/cargurus-nasdaqcarg-posts-q1-cy2026-sales-in-line-with-estimates-but-stock-drops). The Cars.com dealer decline in finding 1 is a separate source pointing the same way.

findings.finding: The guidance arithmetic sets the forward bar. The Q3 guide midpoint ($256M) is +10.3% YoY, slowing from +15% and +13%. The FY +10-13% guide leaves Q4 at $247-274M (+2.5% to +13.8% YoY). The August raise of the FY margin guide (compression cut from 1.5-2.5pp to 0.5-1.5pp) came with a +7.16% move, and the May reiteration of heavy investment came with -8.95%. Narrowing the FY range to the upper half would imply Q4 at or above $261M (+8%+); narrowing to the lower half would imply ~$247-254M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance and margin direction set the sign on the last two prints: +7.16% when the margin guide was raised (Aug 2026) and -8.95% when margin compression was reiterated (May 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: No sourced Q4 consensus was found, so how the guide range will be narrowed cannot be called. It is filed as the line the print turns on, with no sign, so judges can see the range.
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001494259/000119312526338014/carg-ex99_1.htm) carries the revised FY margin guide. Both are company documents.

findings.finding: Regulatory overhang on deal ratings. NYC's DCWP sued CarGurus on 2026-10-15, alleging 'Great/Good Deal' labels exclude mandatory dealer fees (average ~$1,100 markup over 40,000 listings), citing the AI chatbot, and seeking an injunction and civil penalties. California's CARS Act (SB 766), effective 2026-10-01, requires total-price listings. CarGurus has labelled fee-undisclosed listings 'No Rating' since 2026-07-14 and says it will defend vigorously. The call could bring a legal accrual, product changes or Q4 opex commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on prints. The stock was ~$30 in mid-October around the suit and has rallied ~19% since, so the market looked through it.
findings.why_not_priced: It is widely reported and the stock rallied after it, so it is mostly priced. It would matter only if the 10-Q adds an accrual or management says it will change deal ratings nationally.
findings.independence: Auto Remarketing (https://www.autoremarketing.com/ar/technology/cargurus-faces-nyc-lawsuit-over-listings-called-great-deals/) reports the same suit. The CARS Act is a separate source (https://complyauto.com/california-enacts-the-cars-act-overhauling-vehicle-sales-and-leasing-rules/).

findings.finding: This is the first print and first guide under new CFO Matthew Mandel, formerly CFO/COO of Fleetio and ex-Wayfair, effective 2026-10-19. CEO Trevisan had been interim principal financial officer. A new CFO can set a more conservative Q4/FY framework.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CFO-transition print in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since September, so it is pure inference about behaviour, not a number.

findings.finding: The stock rose +22.3% in 20 days and +10.0% in 5 days into the print, from ~$30.3 (10-16) to $35.76. The 11-04 jump came on volume 58% below average, attributed to a sector-wide digital-platform rally with no CarGurus news. The bar for a positive reaction has risen without any company-specific information.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline carries no run-up split. The Feb 2025 print fell -17.13%, the largest move in the history; the run-up before it is not recorded.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is in the price by definition. The claim is that it raised the bar for the release rather than reflecting company information. Against it, the option market pays for upside (skew -25), so this finding is sized small.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline run-up figures (run_up_20d_pct 22.3) are a different source pointing the same way. The Alphastreet 'sector-wide rally' headline (https://news.alphastreet.com/cargurus-surges-10-1-amid-sector-wide-rally/) returned 403 on fetch and is snippet only.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 23% to 9.49M shares (10.7% of shares outstanding, 5.0 days to cover) at the 2026-10-15 settlement, and the 10-30 model estimate is 9.83M. Combined with an upside-paid skew of -25 vol pts, a guide that is merely in line carries squeeze fuel.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No short-interest-conditioned reaction is recorded. Days to cover has ranged 3-9 over the past year.
findings.why_not_priced: The rising short and the upside skew are visible to option traders. Part of the 20-day rally may already be covering, and the 10-30 settlement is not published until 11-10.

findings.finding: Routine insider selling under 10b5-1 plans into the print: COO Samuel Zales sold 10,000 shares at ~$32.33 on 2026-11-02, CPO Ismail Elshareef sold 1,964 at $32.33, and CTO Matthew Quinn sold 3,824 at $29.62 on 10-02. Total insider sales were 83,946 shares over 90 days.
findings.why_not_priced: The sales are pre-planned and public, so the signal is close to nothing.
findings.independence: Investing.com reports the same sale (https://www.investing.com/news/insider-trading-news/cargurus-coo-and-president-samuel-zales-sells-323300-in-shares-93CH-4996727), so it is the same fact.

findings.finding: Monetisation levers beyond listings are still being added. On 2026-09-29 CarGurus launched VIN-level predictive marketing for dealers. PriceVantage, the AI pricing tool launched in late 2025, had reached several hundred paying dealers by Q1 and is sold across tiers. These products support QARSD growth (US +8% in Q2) at a time when the dealer count is flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: QARSD-led beats came with the +7.16% move (Aug 2026). A Barchart item reports +4.6% on the PriceVantage launch day.
findings.why_not_priced: These are product announcements with no revenue number attached, so they are small.
findings.independence: PriceVantage release (https://investors.cargurus.com/node/16761/pdf). It is the company's own material.

findings.finding: Ongoing buybacks support non-GAAP EPS: $29.2M repurchased in Q2 2026, more than 30% of shares retired since Dec 2022, and Q3 EPS guided on 90.0M diluted shares against 94.0M in the Q1 guide. Q2 operating cash flow was $94.6M and FCF $87.7M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats came with mixed reactions: Q2 2026 +$0.05 beat and +7.16%; Q1 2026 in line and -8.95%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is already in the guided share count, so it is mostly priced. The EPS consensus spread ($0.61-0.68) makes the headline beat or miss ambiguous.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-06 CarGurus amended its credit agreement, halving revolving commitments from $400M to $200M and extending maturity. This cuts unused-commitment cost and signals no need for external funding, given $87.7M of quarterly FCF.
findings.why_not_priced: Old and immaterial. Asked what the money buys: nothing is being funded, so it is neutral.

outside_window.finding: FINRA's 2026-10-30 short-interest settlement, modelled at ~9.83M shares (+3.5%), will be published around 2026-11-10, after the exit.
The NYC DCWP lawsuit's court schedule and any penalties fall well after the window.

baseline_tension: Most of what was found leans mildly negative: the peer's dealer-count decline, slowing dealer adds and a sector-driven run-up. That cuts against the upside-paid skew (-25 vol pts) and a rising short of 10.7% of shares. None of it is a decisive company number, so the skew and the squeeze risk keep p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew; crowded short against negatives): Cars.com read-through cut from -0.8 to -0.6, run-up from -0.8 to -0.5, and p_up moved from 47 to 48
Lesson 5 (proxy and inference sized small): the new-CFO conservatism inference cut from -0.3 to -0.1 and the dealer-add trend from -0.5 to -0.4
Pessimism-artefact lesson: the sign balance was re-checked and the positives (SI squeeze fuel, products, buybacks) were left at full size
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): credit-facility reduction confirmed as neutral after asking what the money buys
Lesson 6 (bar): the EPS consensus is disputed ($0.61-0.68), so revenue-against-guide is the bar used and the EPS-dependent finding (buybacks) stays small
